meters.d: Tokens, actions, agent hours. Always measurable; says nothing about value.
A finished unit of work: a case processed, a note signed, a PR merged.
meters.ex: Per case, per document, per task

meters.d: A business result recorded in a system: a resolution, a meeting held, a claim paid.
meters.ex: Per resolution, per meeting, per claim

meters.d: Measured improvement against a baseline or holdout: dollars saved, win rate up.
meters.ex: Share of verified savings, lift bonus

categories.name: Customer support agents
categories.vend: e.g. Sierra, Intercom Fin, Decagon, Zendesk AI
categories.what: Resolves customer conversations end to end across chat, email and voice.
categories.quant: billable = conversations × resolution rate × (1 − reopen rate in window)
categories.market: Per resolution is now standard: Fin $0.99 per outcome; Sierra negotiates per resolution.
categories.metrics: Resolution rate, 7-day reopen rate, CSAT on AI conversations
categories.rule: No human handoff; no reopen in the window; 2% weekly QA sample

lab.attrNote: Event outcome: every resolution is verified, so attribution is 100%.

categories.name: Service intelligence (field service)
categories.vend: e.g. Aquant, ServiceMax, Salesforce Field Service
categories.what: Guides technicians and call centers to the right fix and the right part, and resolves cases remotely.
categories.quant: savings = jobs × (parts per job before − after) × part cost + jobs × (avoidable dispatch rate before − after) × dispatch cost
categories.market: Aquant: each avoidable dispatch costs $200–$1,000+; RATIONAL cut parts per job 34%. Pricing is mostly subscription; a share of verified savings is the outcome path.
categories.metrics: First-time fix rate, parts per job, avoidable dispatch rate, mean time to repair
categories.source: Field service work orders, parts consumption in the ERP, dispatch log
categories.rule: Case closed remotely; no technician dispatched for the same asset in the window; parts savings compared with a 90-day baseline
categories.trail: Work order, asset ID, parts issued, dispatch log

ai: Parts replaced per job, with AI

lab.attrNote: Lift outcome: savings are measured against a holdout of technicians, so only part is credited to the AI.

categories.name: Revenue and sales intelligence
categories.what: Reads calls, emails and CRM to flag deal risk, coach reps, update records and forecast.
categories.quant: value = deals × (win rate with AI − holdout win rate) × deal size + reps × admin hours saved × hourly cost
categories.market: Gong added metered AI credits on top of seats in June 2026. Usage and workflow meters lead; outcome pricing needs a holdout to prove lift.
categories.winLabel: Verification window: deal outcome known within
categories.metrics: Win rate vs. holdout, forecast error, workflows completed, rep hours saved
categories.source: CRM opportunity history, call recordings, frozen forecast snapshots
categories.rule: Rep acted on the flag; deal closed-won; lift measured against a 10% holdout of reps
categories.trail: Flag, rep action, stage history, holdout comparison

base: Admin hours per rep per month, before
ai: Admin hours per rep per month, with AI

lab.attrNote: Lift outcome: half the win-rate gain is credited to the AI after the holdout comparison.

categories.name: AI sales development
categories.what: Researches prospects, writes outreach and books meetings for account executives.
categories.quant: billable = prospects × meeting rate × (1 − no-show and AE-reject rate)
categories.market: $75–$150 per qualified meeting on some enterprise plans; a human SDR costs about $766 per meeting booked.
categories.metrics: Meeting rate, show rate, meeting-to-opportunity rate, cost per meeting
categories.rule: Meeting held and accepted as qualified by the AE in the window
categories.trail: CRM activity, calendar event, AE acceptance stamp

unit: Cost per meeting with a human SDR ($)

lab.attrNote: Event outcome: AE acceptance verifies each meeting; 10% held back for meetings that would have come inbound anyway.

categories.name: IT and employee service
categories.what: Resolves employee requests: access, devices, HR and IT questions.
categories.quant: billable = tickets × auto-resolve rate × (1 − repeat-ticket rate)
categories.market: Mostly seats plus usage; per-resolution offers are emerging. Modeled here.
categories.winLabel: Verification window: no repeat ticket within
categories.metrics: Auto-resolve rate, repeat-ticket rate, time to resolve
categories.rule: Closed without agent touch; no repeat ticket from the same user in the window

unit: Cost of a human-handled ticket ($, assumption)

categories.name: Insurance claims automation
categories.what: Assesses damage, checks coverage and settles simple claims straight through.
categories.quant: billable = claims × straight-through rate × (1 − reopen or supplement rate)
categories.market: Mostly enterprise licenses; per-claim pricing fits because the claim is the unit of work. Modeled here.
categories.winLabel: Verification window: no reopen or supplement within
categories.metrics: Straight-through rate, cycle time, leakage, reopen rate
categories.rule: Paid without adjuster touch; no supplement or reopen in the window
categories.trail: Claim file, photos, coverage check, payment record

unit: Adjuster cost per manual claim ($, assumption)

lab.attrNote: Event outcome; 10% held back for claims that were already simple.

categories.name: Healthcare revenue cycle
categories.what: Works denials, writes appeals and chases payers to recover revenue.
categories.quant: billable = denials worked × overturn rate × recovered dollars × share
categories.market: Vendors often propose a share of the added revenue.
categories.winLabel: Verification window: payment posted, no reversal within
categories.metrics: Clean-claim rate, denial rate, overturn rate, dollars recovered
categories.rule: Payer payment posted; no reversal in the window; price about 4% of a $600 average recovery
categories.trail: Claim ID, appeal packet, remittance record

lab.attrNote: Event outcome; uplift over the prior overturn rate is what is credited.

categories.name: Clinical documentation
categories.vend: e.g. Abridge, Microsoft Dragon Copilot, Suki
categories.what: Listens to the visit and drafts the clinical note for the clinician to sign.
categories.quant: billable = encounters × notes signed without major edits
categories.market: Mostly per clinician; per-encounter pricing ties cost to visit volume. Modeled here.
categories.metrics: Sign-without-edit rate, documentation minutes per visit, after-hours charting
categories.rule: Clinician signs the note with edits under 15% of text in the window
categories.trail: Note version history, signer, edit distance

ai: Documentation minutes per visit, with AI
unit: Value of a clinician minute ($, assumption)

lab.attrNote: Output outcome: each signed note is counted; minutes saved are measured against a pre-launch time study.

categories.name: Legal work
categories.what: Reviews contracts, drafts demands and researches matters for lawyers to approve.
categories.quant: billable = matters processed (per case) or redlines accepted by counsel
categories.market: EvenUp moved to per-case pricing; Harvey and CoCounsel are mostly per seat.
categories.metrics: Review cycle time, share auto-approved, redline acceptance rate
categories.rule: Counsel accepts the AI redline without rewrite in the window

ai: Review hours per contract, with AI

lab.attrNote: Output outcome; hours saved come from matter time records against a baseline quarter.

categories.name: Finance operations
categories.what: Reads invoices, matches them to orders and posts them to the ledger.
categories.quant: billable = invoices × no-touch rate × (1 − human edit before posting)
categories.market: Mostly per invoice volume tiers; true no-touch pricing is an outcome meter. Modeled here.
categories.winLabel: Verification window: no human edit within
categories.metrics: Straight-through rate, exception rate, days payable outstanding
categories.rule: Posted to the ERP with no human edit in the window; three-way match passed
categories.trail: Invoice image, match result, journal entry

unit: Cost of a manually processed invoice ($, assumption)

lab.attrNote: Event outcome, verified in the ERP journal.

categories.name: Software engineering agents
categories.what: Writes, tests and fixes code, and opens pull requests for engineers to review.
categories.quant: billable = agent tasks × PRs merged without rework
categories.market: GitHub moved Copilot plans to usage-based billing in 2026. Heavy token use makes flat seats unprofitable for power users.
categories.metrics: Merge rate, rework rate, cycle time, escaped defects
categories.rule: PR merged by a human reviewer; tests pass; not reverted in the window
categories.trail: PR, review approval, CI run, commit hash
categories.disputeReason: Engineer rewrote most of the diff

unit: Value of a merged PR, 2 hours of engineering ($)

lab.attrNote: Output outcome; 30% held back because engineers would have written some of this code anyway.

categories.name: Marketing and content
categories.what: Generates campaigns, copy and creative, and tests variants.
categories.quant: value = sessions × (conversion with AI − control) × value per conversion
categories.market: Mostly seats and credits; lift-based fees need a control group. Modeled here.
categories.winLabel: Verification window: shipped without rewrite within
categories.metrics: Conversion lift vs. control, approval rate, time to launch
categories.source: Web analytics, marketing automation, approvals in the content system
categories.rule: Asset shipped without rewrite; lift measured with a 10% control audience
categories.trail: Asset version, approver, experiment ID, conversion events

lab.attrNote: Lift outcome: only 40% of the measured lift is credited after the control comparison.

scenarios.name: Ulvane Home
scenarios.d: Outcome-ready: outcome pricing lifts revenue and margin, and every billed outcome traces to a helpdesk record.

scenarios.name: Corvane Outfitters
scenarios.d: A light adopter pays far less under pure outcome. The pane recommends a hybrid floor.

scenarios.name: Halvero Software
scenarios.d: Readiness 43: the gate refuses pure outcome and recommends credits plus a lift bonus.

scenarios.name: Kestane Distribution
scenarios.d: Halve model prices and pass-through credit revenue falls about 40%. Try the token slider.

scenarios.name: Wexmoor Cloud
scenarios.d: A 2-day AE acceptance window triples disputes. Move it to 5 days and watch them fall.

scenarios.name: Norvane Health System
scenarios.d: Outcome-ready; priced at about 4% of recovered dollars.

scenarios.name: Pellwyn Realty
scenarios.d: The vendor bills a platform fee; the customer’s model bill shows separately, striped.

scenarios.name: Estrova Fiber
scenarios.d: Usage feed is 52 days old, so the recommendation is withheld and marked stale.

scenarios.name: Delmora Pharma
scenarios.d: No outcome signal connected: outcome revenue shows as unknown, not $0, and stays out of totals.

scenarios.name: Tarrow Payments
scenarios.d: 600k tokens per task: at $10 per 1M tokens, per-action credit margin turns negative.
